Incorrect attribute name in CF test check_data_types
Whenever I run the CF checker, I get the following message at the start of the results:

```
The following exceptions occured during the cf checker (possibly indicate compliance checker issues):
cf.check_data_types: NetCDF: Attribute not found
```

Running it in verbose mode also prints a stack trace which points to line 271 of cf.py:

```
    for k, v in ds.dataset.variables.iteritems():
        if v.datatype not in [np.character,
                             ...
```

Assuming v is a NetCDF4.Variable object, it should be `v.dtype` instead of `v.datatype`.

5| The definitions given here allow an application to compute dimensional
6| coordinate values from the dimensionless ones and associated variables. The
7| formulas are expressed for a gridpoint (n,k,j,i) where i and j are the
8| horizontal indices, k is the vertical index and n is the time index. A
9| coordinate variable is associated with its definition by the value of the
10| standard_name attribute. The terms in the definition are associated with file
11| variables by the formula_terms attribute. The formula_terms attribute takes a
12| string value, the string being comprised of blank-separated elements of the form
13| "term: variable", where term is a keyword that represents one of the terms in
14| the definition, and variable is the name of the variable in a netCDF file that
15| contains the values for that term. The order of elements is not significant.

17| The gridpoint indices are not formally part of the definitions, but are included
18| to illustrate the indices that might be present in the file variables. For

20| necessarily time dependent in all netCDF files. Also, the definitions are given

106| class DotDict(dict):
107|     """
108|     Subclass of dict that will recursively look up attributes with dot notation.
109|     This is primarily for working with JSON-style data in a cleaner way like javascript.
110|     Note that this will instantiate a number of child DotDicts when you first access attributes;
111|     do not use in performance-critical parts of your code.
112|     """
113| 
114|     def __dir__(self):
115|         return self.__dict__.keys() + self.keys()
116| 
117|     def __getattr__(self, key):
118|         """ Make attempts to lookup by nonexistent attributes also attempt key lookups. """
119|         if self.has_key(key):
120|             return self[key]
121|         import sys
122|         import dis
123|         frame = sys._getframe(1)
124|         if '\x00%c' % dis.opmap['STORE_ATTR'] in frame.f_code.co_code:
125|             self[key] = DotDict()
126|             return self[key]
127| 
128|         raise AttributeError(key)
129| 
130|     def __setattr__(self,key,value):
131|         if key in dir(dict):
132|             raise AttributeError('%s conflicts with builtin.' % key)
133|         if isinstance(value, dict):
134|             self[key] = DotDict(value)
135|         else:
136|             self[key] = value
137| 
138|     def copy(self):
139|         return deepcopy(self)
140| 
141|     def get_safe(self, qual_key, default=None):
142|         """
143|         @brief Returns value of qualified key, such as "system.name" or None if not exists.
144|                 If default is given, returns the default. No exception thrown.
145|         """
146|         value = get_safe(self, qual_key)
147|         if value is None:
148|             value = default
149|         return value

151|     @classmethod
152|     def fromkeys(cls, seq, value=None):
153|         return DotDict(dict.fromkeys(seq, value))

198|         def _get(self, entrynode, attrname, required=False):
199|             vals = entrynode.xpath(attrname)
200|             if len(vals) > 1:
201|                 raise StandardError("Multiple attrs (%s) found" % attrname)
202|             elif required and len(vals) == 0:
203|                 raise StandardError("Required attr (%s) not found" % attrname)

209|         parser = etree.XMLParser(remove_blank_text=True)
210|         self._root = etree.fromstring(resource_text, parser)

212|         # generate and save a list of all standard names in file

214|         self._aliases = [node.get('id') for node in self._root.iter('alias')]

226| 
227|             if len(entryids) != 1:
228|                 raise StandardError("Inconsistency in standard name table, could not lookup alias for %s" % key)
229| 
230|             key = entryids[0].text
231| 
232|         if not key in self._names:
233|             raise KeyError("%s not found in standard name table" % key)
